title: The Pulse — November 13, 2026
tldr: Google shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new daily-driver model built for agentic coding workflows and high-throughput routing. Anthropic announced Claude 4 and filed for IPO. Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents entered private beta, letting teams run the full agent harness on their own infrastructure.
closing: Research: arXiv's overnight listing was empty; no papers in the window.

models.title: Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
models.summary: Google's new workhorse model built for agentic coding, debugging, and high-throughput routing, with 1M token context at $1.50 per million input tokens.
models.why: Directly competes with Claude Sonnet for our agent tooling and multi-step coding workflows; the pricing undercuts Sonnet 4 and the context window fits our EverRaise call processing pipeline that currently uses Claude.

models.title: Claude 4
models.summary: Anthropic announced Claude 4 (details pending; announcement page live).
models.why: We run Claude Sonnet across SalesKick grading, EverRaise agents, and Botterfly's review panels; any capability or pricing change affects every client.

models.title: Claude Self-Hosted Managed Agents
models.summary: Private beta for running the full Claude Managed Agents service (harness, sandboxes, session history) on your own infrastructure, with configurable model routing.
models.why: Solves data residency and compliance requirements for client work; EverRaise and Life International both asked about on-premises agent hosting.

releases.title: Node.js v27.0.0-alpha.0.1.0
releases.summary: Node 27 alpha with crypto X.509 generation, CSR support, subprocess.timedOut, and coalesced DNS lookups.
releases.why: We run Node across Pipeline services and Chrysalis; alpha releases signal breaking changes to watch before they land in Current.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.79.0
releases.summary: Langfuse adds OpenRouter, xAI, and Vercel AI Gateway as generally-available AI gateway providers, plus audit logging for MCP tool read-access.
releases.why: We use Langfuse for tracing on SalesKick and EverRaise; OpenRouter gateway support means unified tracing across our multi-model routing.

hackernews.title: Anthropic IPO
hackernews.summary: Anthropic filed for IPO; registration page live, 857 points and 825 comments on HN.
hackernews.why: We bet heavily on Claude across every client; an IPO means financial transparency and potentially more predictable pricing and service terms.

hackernews.title: Foundation Models framework
hackernews.summary: Apple's new Foundation Models framework for integrating language models into iOS, iPadOS, and macOS apps (162 points).
hackernews.why: Worth knowing; no direct use for us yet, but if a client asks for on-device inference on Apple platforms, this is the native path.

hackernews.title: Humble Bundle security breach via AI-generated code
hackernews.summary: Humble Bundle's security compromised after shipping AI-generated code without review (373 points, 222 comments).
hackernews.why: Cautionary tale for our wehshi review process; the thread documents how unchecked agent output reached production and broke auth.

hackernews.title: 22-year-old Postgres type-confusion primitive turned into RCE
hackernews.summary: Researcher turned a decades-old Postgres type mismatch into remote code execution (CVE-2026-6460, 156 points).
hackernews.why: We use Postgres on SalesKick and several Pipeline clients; check the CVE and patch if affected.

x_posts.title: shadcn introduces UI SDK for agents
x_posts.summary: shadcn introduced UI SDK (github.com/vercel-labs/ui): component abstractions for agents building and using interfaces, with shared logic for selection, focus, and keyboard navigation; upcoming 'agentic features' teased (3,226 likes).
x_posts.why: We build agent UIs for SalesKick and Pipeline clients; if UI SDK handles the repetitive accessibility and state logic, it could speed up our React work.

x_posts.title: Sebastian Raschka on Nemotron and open-weight training recipes
x_posts.summary: Raschka hopes Nvidia's Nemotron keeps going; notes that open training recipes and data would be harder to replace than the models themselves (610 likes).
x_posts.why: Worth knowing; no direct use for us yet, but training transparency is the moat for reproducible research.
